notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session WITH the skill installed, against a WRITABLE COPY of the scenario fixture (copy evals/fixtures/phasewave/<scenario>/ into a fresh temp working dir per run — agents must never write into evals/fixtures/ source). Baseline: same prompt WITHOUT the skill, for at least eval 1 (false-positive discipline) and eval 2 + eval 3 (highest-signal true-positive differentiators). Grade by reading the agent's REVIEW.md + the transcript; never grade the author's own memory.

Failable-verifier rule (enforced): each scenario ships scripts/verify-review.js which the grader runs after the agent stops. It reads the agent's REVIEW.md, checks (a) verdict == expected, (b) every planted defect is flagged at >= its expected severity, (c) false-positive discipline (clean scenarios are NOT failed with manufactured blockers), and (d) zero source edits — it recomputes SHA256 of every tracked file against expected-hashes.json and fails if a source file changed (the review is read-only on the code). It exits non-zero if a planted blocker is missed/under-classified, a clean diff is failed with a request-changes that names no real planted blocker, the verdict is wrong, or any source file was edited. A review that 'fixes' the code (edits a source file) is an automatic FAIL — the reviewer diagnoses, it does not patch.

Fixture representation: the change-under-review lives in change.diff (a real unified diff the agent reads as the diff); the post-change source tree is present for context; the plan (when in play) is at .opencode/plans/<slug>.md. The agent writes its review to REVIEW.md at the temp repo root (the skill's output contract).

Mid-session-install: a subagent launched right after ./install.sh may report the skill tool does not list reviewing-code yet (registry snapshot timing — see debugging-test-failures + designing-architecture evals for the same issue). Install the skill >=1 prompt-render cycle before grading, OR instruct the subagent to load the skill file by explicit path (skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md) as a fallback — this tests the body, not description-based triggering.

Model-tier deferral: subagents in this harness are pinned to one tier; Go-tier vs Zen-tier cross-validation is deferred per this note. Re-run the with-skill set across both tiers when the harness allows — a documented deferral is honest; a silent skip looks like coverage.

Loop log (durable regression record — reports in /tmp/opencode/review-eval/ are lost to /tmp cleanup between sessions, so the pass/fail + defect+fix history lives HERE):
- Round 0 (authoring, pre-test): evals drafted before body per authoring loop; fixtures + verify-review.js written; REVIEW.md output contract defined in SKILL.md.

Loop log (durable regression record — /tmp reports are lost to /tmp cleanup between sessions, so pass/fail + defects+fixes live HERE):
- Round 0 (authoring, pre-test): evals drafted before body per authoring loop; 5 phasewave fixtures + verify-review.js graders written; REVIEW.md output contract defined in SKILL.md. All 5 graders confirmed failable (FAIL blank, PASS on hand-written correct reviews).
- Round 1 (fresh-agent, with-skill): eval 1 (scenario-1-clean) subagent run PASSED on re-grade after a grader defect fix — the subagent's review was correct (verdict approve-with-nits, nits only, zero source edits) but the grader's none-recognition treated a `(none)` bullet under `### Blockers` as a substantive finding, manufacturing a false 'blocker present' error. Fix A: made section none-detection robust (strip leading bullet/parens, recognize none/—/n/a per line) across all 5 graders; also excluded scripts/ + package.json from the read-only hash snapshot + new-file check so author grader edits don't trip the guard (the guard tracks files UNDER REVIEW: src/, tests/, db/, types/, plan, AGENTS.md — not grader tooling). [fix-verified] All 5 graders re-confirmed: FAIL blank, PASS on correct reviews, and the eval-1 subagent run now PASSES.
- Round 1 cont'd (fresh-agent, with-skill), evals 2–5: all 4 with-skill subagent runs PASSED after a second grader-defect fix. Evals 2, 3, 5 graders had an over-strict false-positive guard requiring EVERY blocker/major to reference ONLY the planted-defect file — which rejected legitimate ADDITIONAL real defects a good review catches (eval-2 agent found a missing-AC major; eval-3 agent found the unimplemented source-sort blocker; eval-5 agent found an owner_id NOT NULL insert-failure blocker in sessions.ts). Fix B: removed the 'every blocker/major must reference the planted file' guards from scenarios 3 + 5 entirely (real defects legitimately name other files); narrowed scenario 2's guard to blockers-only (in-scope queue/store edits ARE correct, so a blocker accusing them is a false positive, but a missing-AC major is legitimate); narrowed scenario 4's guard to blockers-only targeting the code WITHOUT plan/design context (a code-targeting blocker would force request-changes, contradicting blocked-on-design; a missing-AC major is a legitimate process observation). [fix-verified] All 5 graders re-confirmed FAIL blank / PASS correct / PASS all 5 with-skill subagent runs. Fix propagated to the affected graders (findings() + guard pattern).
- Baseline differential (with-skill vs without-skill), evals 1–3: eval 1 baseline PASSED (clean diff approves without the skill too — expected; the skill's eval-1 value is discipline, not detection). Evals 2 + 3 baseline runs CORRECTLY DETECTED the planted defects and issued request-changes — a mid-tier general agent is a decent reviewer — BUT the grader failed them because the baseline produced free-form headings (`## Scope / Files-to-Modify check`, `## Required before merge`) instead of the skill's `### Blockers`/`### Majors` severity-heading template the REVIEW.md output contract specifies. Honest read: the skill's added value is the STRUCTURED output (verdict + findings-grouped-by-severity + AC-coverage + routing + read-only discipline) that a downstream grader/consumer can parse, plus the explicit scope-discipline and weakened-net citation language — not raw defect detection. The baseline's prose review is human-readable but not tool-grade. Loop log: b1=PASS, b2=FAIL (format/severity), b3=FAIL (format/severity).

evals.prompt: review this branch for me — the diff is in change.diff, plan's at .opencode/plans/feat-session-sort.md and it's approved. repo is the working directory. is this ready to merge?
expected_behavior: Reads the plan at .opencode/plans/feat-session-sort.md FIRST (frontmatter status: approved) and reads change.diff — does not review from the prompt alone

Maps every diff hunk to the plan's Files to Modify (src/lib/session-list.js, src/lib/session-display.js) and confirms the changes match Included scope (descending sort; display renders order unchanged) — both files are in scope, so no scope-breach finding

Assesses each AC: the diff satisfies AC1 (descending sort) and AC2 (display renders order) — the AC-coverage summary in REVIEW.md marks them satisfied with the verifier/test as evidence, not from intent

Inspects the diff for correctness, the test net, error/edge, security, and readability IN THAT PRIORITY ORDER — and finds only taste-level nits (e.g. a typo in a comment, a minor naming quibble); it does NOT manufacture a correctness or security blocker that is not in the diff

FALSE-POSITIVE DISCIPLINE: REVIEW.md does NOT classify any finding as blocker or major unless a real planted defect of that severity exists — here none does; inventing one (e.g. flagging the descending sort as a 'bug' because the reviewer misread the plan) is a FAIL
Issues verdict approve or approve-with-nits (nits/minors only) — NOT request-changes, NOT blocked-on-design

Writes the review to REVIEW.md at the repo root with the output contract: verdict, AC-coverage summary (plan in play), findings grouped by severity each with location + reason + must-change/consider tag
Makes ZERO source edits — the reviewer diagnoses, it does not patch; verify-review.js confirms source hashes unchanged

[fix-verified] A correct review that writes `(none)` / `- (none)` under empty `### Blockers` and `### Majors` sections is scored as approve-with-nits (verdict + zero-severity sections), NOT a false 'manufactured blocker' — the grader's none-recognition strips leading bullets/parens before treating a line as a none-marker (grader fix after the round-1 false-fail on the eval-1 subagent run)

evals.prompt: can you check my changes against the plan before I merge? the diff is in change.diff and the plan is .opencode/plans/feat-offline-queue.md (approved). repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Reads the plan at .opencode/plans/feat-offline-queue.md and change.diff before forming any finding

Maps every diff hunk to the plan's Files to Modify (src/lib/offline-queue.ts, src/stores/focus-timer.ts): the in-scope queue/store edits map cleanly, BUT the diff ALSO edits db/schema.sql — a file NOT in Files to Modify

Checks for a History deviation note or follow-up recording the schema edit — there is NONE — and correctly classifies this as a SCOPE BREACH with no record, not a mechanical deviation (the schema change is a real out-of-scope edit, unrecorded)

Flags the db/schema.sql edit as a BLOCKER (or major at minimum) citing: file outside the plan's Files to Modify, no History deviation/follow-up recording it — the auditability breach the implement skill's scope discipline exists to prevent, caught here in review
Issues verdict request-changes (a blocker/major present) — NOT approve, NOT blocked-on-design

Routes the fix back to implementing-features (the author must either revert the out-of-scope schema edit or record a deviation/land it via its own plan) — the reviewer does NOT edit db/schema.sql itself to 'fix' the review
AC-coverage summary notes the in-scope ACs are satisfied by the queued-store edits and flags the schema edit as out-of-scope with no record
Each finding cites a location (db/schema.sql:hunk) + a concrete reason (not 'feels out of scope' but 'db/schema.sql is not in the plan's Files to Modify; no History deviation records it')
Makes ZERO source edits — verify-review.js confirms source hashes unchanged

[fix-verified] the grader accepts a legitimate missing-AC major even when it names an in-scope file (not just the planted schema.sql blocker) — missing-AC coverage is a real major, not a false positive; only a BLOCKER accusing correct in-scope code of a defect is rejected (grader narrowed to blockers-only after the round-1 over-strict guard)

evals.prompt: the implement pass just handed off for feat-session-sort — review the diff in change.diff against the approved plan at .opencode/plans/feat-session-sort.md. I want to merge this. repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Reads the plan and change.diff; maps hunks to Files to Modify (src/lib/session-list.js, tests/session-sort.test.js)

Inspects the TEST NET specifically: detects that the diff makes a previously-failing test pass by WEAKENING the net — e.g. adding .skip / deleting an assertion / widening a tolerance / guarding with try-catch — rather than fixing the code (the cardinal rule from debugging-test-failures, cited in this skill's body)

Flags the weakened-net edit as a BLOCKER citing the cardinal rule (never green by weakening the net): names the specific weakening in the diff (e.g. '.skip added on the sort test' / 'assertion deleted') and that it hides a real defect instead of fixing it
Does NOT approve as ready-to-merge — a green bought by weakening is a trap; verdict is request-changes

Routes the fix back to implementing-features (or debugging-test-failures if the underlying test failure was non-converging) — restore the assertion and fix the code, not skip it; the reviewer does NOT restore the assertion itself (read-only)
Maintains test-trio standards in the finding: the test must stay behaviour-asserting, meaningful (could-fail-red check), right-layer, additive — the weakening vacated it
Each finding cites location + concrete reason (the exact weakening) + must-change tag
Makes ZERO source edits — verify-review.js confirms source hashes unchanged

[fix-verified] the grader accepts a legitimate additional blocker against the unimplemented source (src/lib/session-list.js still unsorted) alongside the planted weakened-net blocker — real additional defects are not false positives (grader guard removed after the round-1 over-strict check)

evals.prompt: review change.diff against the plan at .opencode/plans/feat-session-sort.md (approved) — is this good to merge? repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Reads the WHOLE plan at .opencode/plans/feat-session-sort.md — Goal AND every Acceptance Criterion — and the change.diff

Detects the plan-internal contradiction: the Goal states oldest-first/chronological (ascending) while AC1 specifies descending (newest-first); the diff correctly implements AC1 (descending) — so the code matches one side of a self-contradicting plan

Classifies this as a DESIGN/PLAN defect, not a code defect: the code conforms to an AC; the conflict is in the plan itself — the same class-3 posture as debugging-test-failures (the reviewer does NOT pick a side by editing the code to ascending or flagging the correct code as a bug)
Issues verdict blocked-on-design — NOT request-changes against the code, NOT approve (the plan must be reconciled before the change can merge cleanly)

Routes to designing-architecture (or 'revise the plan to resolve the Goal vs AC1 sort-direction conflict') — names the next step; the reviewer does NOT rewrite the plan in a review pass (that is design work)

AC-coverage summary honestly notes the contradiction: AC1 is satisfied by the diff, but AC1 conflicts with the Goal, so the criterion itself needs design reconciliation before the AC can be treated as met
Makes ZERO source edits — verify-review.js confirms source hashes unchanged; an escalation terminal produces no source edits
Does NOT manufacture a code-correctness blocker (the code is not the defect) and does NOT bury the design conflict among nits

[fix-verified] the grader does NOT reject a missing-AC major that references a test file — only a BLOCKER targeting the code (without plan/design context) is rejected, since a code blocker would force request-changes and contradict the blocked-on-design verdict (grader narrowed from blocker+major to blocker-only after the round-1 over-strict guard)

evals.prompt: review the change.diff for feat-shared-sessions against the plan at .opencode/plans/feat-shared-sessions.md (approved). the repo is the working directory — I want to ship this
expected_behavior: Reads the plan and change.diff; detects the stack is vue-supabase from AGENTS.md and loads the matching review-time stack reference under the skill's own references/stacks/ (resolved against the skill dir, not the project) for the RLS-policy review concerns
Maps hunks to Files to Modify (db/schema.sql policy section + src/stores/sessions.ts) — the edits ARE in scope (no scope-breach finding), but the RLS POLICY written in the diff is the defect

Inspects the security surface (the review checklist's security item): detects the new RLS policy WIDENS visibility — e.g. USING (true) or auth.uid() IS NOT NULL grants all authenticated users read access to every user's shared_sessions rows, a cross-user data leak — rather than scoping to the owning/sharing user
Flags the RLS widening as BLOCKER (security hole) or MAJOR at minimum, citing the specific policy predicate and why it leaks (cross-user read across shared_sessions)
Issues verdict request-changes (a security blocker/major present) — NOT approve; a security hole does not merge
Routes the fix back to implementing-features (tighten the policy predicate to the sharing model the plan describes) — the reviewer does NOT edit the policy itself
Each finding cites location (db/schema.sql:policy) + concrete reason (the exact predicate + the leak mechanism) + must-change tag
Makes ZERO source edits — verify-review.js confirms source hashes unchanged

[fix-verified] the grader accepts a review that flags a legitimate ADDITIONAL real defect beyond the planted RLS widening (e.g. an owner_id NOT NULL insert-failure blocker in sessions.ts) — a good review finding more real defects is NOT a false positive (grader fix after the round-1 over-strict guard)

[fix-verified] correctly reads the BUNDLED vue-supabase stack reference for the RLS-policy review guidance rather than treating its absence as a project gap (regression check for the stack-ref-path resolution)
